title: Fast-track hiring: skill probe, panel flow & Day 1 compact setup checklist
content:
Purpose:
This compact working doc defines a repeatable, conservative fast-track flow for hiring experienced individual contributors (typically lateral hires and senior ICs) where time-to-offer and Day 1 productivity matter. It bundles: a short technical skill-probe (home or take-home), a structured 90-minute panel interview flow, and a minimal Day 1 provisioning + onboarding checklist so hires can be productive in week 1.

When to use:
- Candidate has strong resume signals (senior+ IC from similar stack) and sponsor asks for 7–14 day cycle.
- Role is non-manager IC (senior engineer, infra, SRE, devtools).
- Hiring manager commits to fast feedback and paired onboarding buddy.

Skill probe (goal: 60–90 minute evaluator time):
- Option A (take-home light): single-file repo with 2 small tasks (one correctness + one optimization) estimated 60m. Deliverable: PR or gist and 10–15 minute explainer note.
- Option B (live paired): 45–60m remote pair-programming on a focused bug/feature in the language of hire. Use shared editor and recording off by default.
- Grading: submit a one-page scorecard (see rubric below) within 24 hours of probe completion.

Panel interview flow (90 minutes total):
1) 5m intro - recruiter / host: expectations, timeboxes
2) 35m system design/architecture - hiring manager + senior engineer: evaluate trade-offs, constraints, and rollout strategy
3) 25m take-home walkthrough or live coding deep-dive - peer engineer: correctness, clarity, debugging, test strategy
4) 15m behavioral + collaboration scenarios - cross-functional partner (e.g., product or infra)
5) 10m Q&A + close - interviewer(s) summarize next steps

Scoring rubric (single-page quick matrix, 1–5 where 3 = meets bar):
- Technical correctness (1-5): code is correct, tests or mental checking used
- System thinking (1-5): identifies constraints, tradeoffs, failure modes
- Ownership & tradeoffs (1-5): prioritization, incremental rollout, observability plan
- Communication (1-5): writes/speaks clearly, scopes ambiguity, asks clarifying Qs
- Collaboration fit (1-5): cross-team empathy, async docs habit
- Overall hire recommendation: Strong Hire / Hire / Consider / No Hire

Quick decision template (to be filled by hiring manager within 48h):
- Probe format used: live/take-home
- Average rubric score: X.X
- Key risks (top 3): e.g., limited infra exposure, unfamiliar language, leadership gaps
- Must-haves for success in first 90 days: specific onboarding tasks (see Day 1 list)
- Offer target (comp band + sign-on) and timeline: agree by date

Day 1 compact provisioning & onboarding checklist (goal: full dev loop by EOD Day 1):
Pre-Day-1 (People Ops / IT / Manager actions, complete before new hire local start):
- Laptop imaged and shipped with expected OS and dev toolchain installed (list: git, docker, python/pyenv, node, editor)
- Okta/SSO account pre-provisioned and access to /internal/* repos granted (temporary = read on all repos; manager to request narrower perms post-day2)
- Slack account created and placed into #eng-onboarding, #team-[x], and #general.
- Access to ticketing (Jira) and CI dashboards (Grafana/Datadog) provisioned with viewer role.
- Onboarding calendar: Day 1 9am welcome, 10am infra overview, 1pm buddy pairing, 3pm must-fix small task assigned.

Day 1 (Manager & Buddy):
- 09:00 – Quick welcome + org chart + product context (15m)
- 09:30 – HR / Benefits intro (remote link provided in calendar)
- 10:00 – Security + acceptable use, keys, KMS basics (15m)
- 10:30 – Dev environment walkthrough: clone repo, run tests, run local dev server (buddy pairs)
- 13:00 – Assigned tiny starter issue (non-blocking): build -> run -> open PR template (goal: open a PR by EOD)
- 15:00 – Intro to team rituals and CI/CD pipeline + release cadence (30m)
- 16:00 – 1:1 with manager: immediate 30/60/90 expectations and success metrics (30m)
- 17:15 – End-of-day sync: checklist signoff and quick retrospective (20m)

Post-Day-1 week plan (manager to assign in first 48h):
- Day 2–3: finish 90m onboarding deep dives (data flow, infra runbooks, observability playbook)
- Week 1: two code reviews expected, one feature branch merged with buddy support
- Week 2: owner of small feature/bug, demo to team in retro

Operational notes & guardrails:
- Use fast-track only for hires where sponsor (hiring manager) guarantees interviewer availability for decision within 48h of final interview. If any step slips >72h, revert to regular hiring workflow.
- Compensation approvals must be requested pre-offer; for fast-track roles, hiring manager to submit comp paperwork in parallel with interviews.
- For remote hires in regulated markets, include security/compliance lead in offer loop.

Appendix: example short probe (copy/paste):
Task: Implement a small in-memory LRU cache with TTL and provide a test that demonstrates eviction and TTL behavior. Time budget: 60 minutes. Deliverable: single-file implementation + test + 1-paragraph note on complexity and failure modes.

Notes & open questions (working):
- Should we standardize one language per hiring queue to simplify test setup? (Maya to survey infra team)
- Automation: can IT accept a CSV to bulk-provision Okta groups to speed pre-day-1? (Diego to spike)

Slack threads / tickets to reference:
- #people-ops-hiring (thread: fast-track-pilot)
- HR-3421 (Jira) — fast-track pilot approvals

If approved, small pilot to run across 3 teams in Q4 2025. Feedback cadence: weekly retrospective with interviewers after each closed loop (offer / reject) for 6 weeks.
